question: What is the main genetic material found inside the HIV virus?

options.A: Ribosomal RNA
options.B: Plasmid DNA
options.C: Single-stranded RNA
options.D: Double-stranded DNA

explanation: Think of HIV as an RNA virus! It carries two strands of single-stranded RNA, which it uses to make DNA once inside your body's cells. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h1)

question: A young teenager is diagnosed with a rare ovarian tumor that starts from the cells that make eggs. What type of tumor is this?

options.A: Germ cell tumor
options.B: Stromal tumor
options.C: Squamous cell tumor
options.D: Epithelial tumor

explanation: Great thinking! Germ cell tumors arise from the egg-producing cells and are more commonly seen in younger patients.

question: What physical sign on a head bandage might make you suspect a leak of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)?

options.A: A foul-smelling green discharge with pus
options.B: Complete dryness with no visible fluid stains
options.C: Bright red blood soaking through the entire bandage
options.D: A clear yellow halo surrounding a spot of blood

explanation: CSF mixed with blood is clever—it separates on dressings, forming that distinct watery ring or halo right around the blood spot!

question: Which position usually helps relieve sharp chest pain for a patient with acute pericarditis?

options.A: Sitting back with legs elevated
options.B: Lying flat on the back
options.C: Sitting upright and leaning forward
options.D: Lying flat on the left side

explanation: Leaning forward pulls the heart away from the inflamed sac around it, reducing painful rubbing. Simple and good to know for clinical practice!

question: How does pulling the neck bones back into alignment help the spinal canal?

options.A: Seal cerebrospinal fluid leaks inside the neck
options.B: Speed up the healing of torn skin tissues
options.C: Prevent the patient from developing a respiratory infection
options.D: Relieve pressure on the spinal cord by creating space

explanation: Great thinking. When the bones snap back into their correct spot, it opens up the spinal canal and takes dangerous pressure off the spinal cord.

question: What is the main purpose of the evaluation step in the nursing process?

options.A: To write the initial medical diagnosis for the patient chart
options.B: To perform the physical head-to-toe baseline assessment
options.C: To administer emergency medications during a crisis
options.D: To determine if the patient met the established care goals

explanation: Exactly! Evaluation is where you check the patient's progress to see if your care plan actually worked or needs a tweak.

question: What is it called when the ductus arteriosus fails to close normally after a baby is born?

options.A: Patent ductus arteriosus
options.B: Umbilical cord rupture
options.C: Hepatic duct closure
options.D: Foramen ovale stenosis

explanation: You've got this! 'Patent' simply means open. If that little bypass tube stays open past the newborn period, we call it a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA). [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h8)

question: What happens to C3 complement protein levels in the blood during active Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: They rise to very high levels
options.B: They fluctuate every few hours
options.C: They drop below normal levels
options.D: They remain completely unchanged

explanation: Think of C3 proteins as defense workers that get completely used up and depleted by the ongoing immune battle in the kidneys, leaving low levels in the blood test.

question: How can severe physical or emotional stress lead to spaced-out periods (oligomenorrhoea)?

options.A: By suppressing hypothalamic release of GnRH
options.B: By causing immediate scarring of the uterine wall
options.C: By destroying ovarian follicles directly
options.D: By blocking estrogen receptors in the liver

explanation: Stress triggers hormones like cortisol, which temporarily puts a pause on the hypothalamus releasing GnRH. Without that signal, ovulation gets delayed!

question: What medical term describes how severe or dangerous a disease is when caused by an infectious agent?

options.A: Contagiosity
options.B: Virulence
options.C: Pathogenicity
options.D: Infectivity

explanation: Think of virulence as the 'punch' a germ packs. It tells us how severe or even fatal the resulting disease can be to the host.

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the actual production of milk in the alveoli?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Prolactin stimulates the glandular cells of the alveoli to synthesize breast milk. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h8)

question: What electrolyte abnormality is a key feature of Tumor Lysis Syndrome?

options.A: High potassium
options.B: Low phosphate
options.C: High calcium
options.D: Low sodium

explanation: When massive numbers of cancer cells burst open, they flood the bloodstream with intracellular potassium, causing hyperkalemia. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h2)

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Infection, immunity, and recovery
options.B: Source, symptom, and treatment
options.C: Vector, parasite, and climate
options.D: Agent, host, and environment

explanation: It's all about the agent causing the trouble, the host carrying it, and the environment bringing them together!

question: Which serious brain condition can result from severe oxygen deprivation during labour?

options.A: Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy
options.B: Neonatal physiological jaundice
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Transient tachypnoea of the newborn

explanation: Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy is brain damage caused by lack of oxygen and blood flow to the brain around the time of birth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h7)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take when a patient shows signs of severe drug toxicity?

options.A: Stop the administration of the offending medication
options.B: Increase the intravenous fluid rate without a doctor's order
options.C: Document the event in the patient's chart at the end of the shift
options.D: Ask the patient to walk around the room to stay awake

explanation: Stopping the drug source prevents any more of the toxic substance from entering the patient's system. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h7)

question: Which sign is most characteristic of a tension pneumothorax?

options.A: Frequent coughing with clear, thin mucus production
options.B: A slow and steady heart rate with warm, dry skin
options.C: Absent breath sounds on the affected side of the chest
options.D: Equal and bilateral chest expansion during breathing

explanation: Trapped air collapses the lung and prevents air entry, resulting in absent or significantly diminished breath sounds on that side. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h4)

question: Why are community health nurses in a great position to promote cancer prevention?

options.A: They are the only healthcare professionals permitted to diagnose tumors
options.B: They hold exclusive authority over national public health budgets
options.C: They interact directly with individuals and families on a regular basis
options.D: They spend all their time working inside high-tech molecular laboratories

explanation: Because nurses interact regularly with everyday people and families, they are perfectly placed to teach about risk factors and encourage healthy habits. Well done! [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h7)

question: A patient is prescribed a sustained-release capsule for chronic pain. What must the nurse tell the patient about taking this medication?

options.A: Swallow the capsule whole without chewing or crushing
options.B: Chew the capsule thoroughly before swallowing with water
options.C: Crush the capsule into food if swallowing is difficult
options.D: Open the shell and dissolve the powder in hot water

explanation: Crushing or chewing sustained-release medications destroys their special mechanism and causes a dangerous, immediate release of the entire drug dose. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when treating young children with HIV?

options.A: Calculating doses carefully according to the child's exact weight
options.B: Using dispersible or pleasant-tasting liquid formulations
options.C: Involving caregivers closely in daily medication administration
options.D: Using standard adult high-dose tablets without breaking them

explanation: Correct! Adult tablets are not safe or accurate for kids. Children need syrups, dispersible tablets, and exact weight-based dosing.

question: Which nursing activity is vital for long-term cancer survivors?

options.A: Administering initial chemotherapy cycles in the acute ward
options.B: Performing major reconstructive surgeries in the clinic
options.C: Prescribing high-dose narcotic pain medications
options.D: Monitoring for late-appearing side effects of treatment

explanation: Even years later, survivors can develop delayed side effects affecting their heart or lungs, making watchful nursing care essential.

question: Which standard lab test checks a patient's hemoglobin and hematocrit levels directly?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Coagulation screen
options.C: Basic metabolic profile
options.D: Liver function panel

explanation: The good old Full Blood Count (or Complete Blood Count) is your go-to test for looking at red cells, hemoglobin, and all things blood-related in the ward!

question: What is the main goal of surgery when treating a patient with a torn heart muscle?

options.A: Replacing the damaged heart with an artificial mechanical pump
options.B: Directly suturing the tear and relieving pressure in the pericardium
options.C: Removing the entire outer layer of the pericardial sac permanently
options.D: Tying off the coronary arteries to prevent further blood loss

explanation: The surgeon's priority is to stitch up the heart muscle tear and open the sac to drain trapped blood so the heart can beat freely again.

question: How does progesterone help protect the growing baby from the mother's immune system?

options.A: By destroying white blood cells that enter the uterine cavity
options.B: By acting as an immune modulator to prevent tissue rejection
options.C: By creating a thick physical barrier of mucus around the fetus
options.D: By lowering the mother's total body temperature significantly

explanation: Clever, right? Progesterone gently tweaks the local immune response so the mother's body recognizes the baby as family instead of attacking it as a foreign body.

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for preparing the lining of the womb for implantation?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Well done! Progesterone takes the lead in the second half of the cycle, making the womb lining thick and cozy for a potential pregnancy.

question: Which chemical substance is primarily responsible for causing uterine contractions and pain in dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Adrenaline
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Prostaglandins

explanation: Prostaglandins build up in the uterine lining and stimulate strong contractions of the uterine muscle, leading to cramping pain. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h2)

question: What does 'displacement volume' mean when reconstituting a powdered medication in a vial?

options.A: The leftover medicine discarded after the injection is given
options.B: The speed at which the plunger pushes the fluid out
options.C: The amount of liquid lost through evaporation during mixing
options.D: The extra space taken up by the dry powder inside the liquid

explanation: Dry powder adds physical volume to the vial when mixed with a liquid, which can change the final concentration if not accounted for. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is a very common early physical sign in someone developing CJD?

options.A: Involuntary muscle jerks
options.B: High fever and sweating
options.C: Severe joint swelling
options.D: Yellowing of the skin

explanation: Spot on! Sudden, involuntary muscle jerking (called myoclonus) is a classic physical sign as the disease progresses.

question: What is the normal pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: Keep this number locked in your memory! A pH of 7.35 to 7.45 keeps body enzymes working smoothly and cells happy.

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of cervical irritation?

options.A: Chemical exposure from scented douches
options.B: Mechanical friction during intercourse
options.C: Infectious microorganisms like chlamydia
options.D: Eating high-sodium processed foods

explanation: You got it! Eating salty food won't irritate your cervix, but harsh chemicals, friction, and infections definitely can.

question: Through which tiny pathways do drugs leave the peritoneal cavity and enter the body?

options.A: Capillaries and lymphatic channels
options.B: Arterial valves and heart chambers
options.C: Bile ducts and the gall bladder
options.D: Ureters and the urinary bladder

explanation: Correct! The web of tiny blood capillaries and lymph channels in the peritoneal membrane helps pick up the drugs and carry them where they need to go. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h3)

question: How do acquired bleeding problems differ from inherited conditions like hemophilia?

options.A: Acquired disorders develop later in life due to illnesses or deficiencies
options.B: Inherited disorders only show up during major surgery in adulthood
options.C: Inherited disorders can be cured easily with simple vitamin supplements
options.D: Acquired disorders only affect red blood cells instead of platelets

explanation: While inherited conditions are passed down in your genes from birth, acquired disorders pop up later in life because of illness, poor nutrition, or certain medications.

question: Which of these is a chemical barrier part of our innate defense?

options.A: Cytotoxic T-cell activation
options.B: Keratin in the outer skin layer
options.C: Lysozyme in tears and saliva
options.D: Antibodies produced by plasma cells

explanation: You're right! Lysozyme is a natural germ-killer found in our tears and saliva that breaks open bacterial walls.

question: What is an important safety action when caring for a patient who is actively having a tonic-clonic seizure?

options.A: Immediately give a large glass of water to prevent dehydration
options.B: Hold the patient's arms and legs tightly to stop all shaking
options.C: Keep emergency equipment like suction and oxygen close at hand
options.D: Force a padded wooden tongue depressor between the teeth

explanation: Safety first! Keeping suction and oxygen nearby helps you manage their airway once the shaking stops. Never try to hold their limbs down or force anything into their mouth.

question: What does the term 'medicalization' mean when talking about female genital mutilation?

options.A: Treating FGM infections in a hospital setting
options.B: Having a trained healthcare worker perform the cutting procedure
options.C: Doing scientific research on how common the practice is
options.D: Using modern pain relief during traditional cutting

explanation: You're on point! Medicalization refers to the harmful practice of health workers performing FGM under the false belief that clinical tools make it safe.

question: Why does a lack of health awareness stop patients from insisting on safe injections?

options.A: They have enough money to buy private syringes
options.B: They prefer taking bitter oral medications instead
options.C: They understand hospital sterilization protocols fully
options.D: They do not know what hazards to look out for

explanation: You nailed it. If a patient doesn't know the risks, they won't know what dangerous practices to watch out for or what to demand.

question: Why do nurses care so much about spotting workplace hazards early?

options.A: It stops short-term injuries and long-term chronic illnesses
options.B: It guarantees higher daily wages for industrial workers
options.C: It removes the need for personal protective equipment
options.D: It completely eliminates all physical labor in factories

explanation: Catching risks early means we can protect workers before they get seriously hurt. Prevention is always better than cure!

question: Which oral antifungal drug is a favorite for treating urinary yeast infections because it travels well into the urine?

options.A: Clotrimazole
options.B: Fluconazole
options.C: Ketoconazole
options.D: Miconazole

explanation: Fluconazole is easily absorbed and concentrates nicely right where it's needed in the urinary tract. Great choice for a quick pill!

question: What is the primary advantage of mobile health clinics in reproductive health outreach?

options.A: Providing free cars to every pregnant woman
options.B: Replacing all permanent hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Eliminating the need for community health education
options.D: Bringing family planning supplies directly to remote villages

explanation: Mobile clinics bridge the geographical gap by bringing essential services closer to people who live far from standard health facilities. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: Why is continuous, long-term monitoring so essential when caring for patients with degenerative conditions?

options.A: It completely stops the underlying genetic mutation from spreading
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: It guarantees the patient will regain full physical strength
options.D: It helps catch slow, steady declines and new complications early

explanation: Because these diseases creep up slowly over time, keeping a close eye on the patient helps us catch new problems right away and step in to help.

question: What core toxicological principle states that virtually any substance can act as a poison if the quantity is large enough?

options.A: All chemicals are inherently lethal
options.B: The route determines toxicity
options.C: Metabolism prevents all toxicity
options.D: The dose makes the poison

explanation: Toxicology teaches that safety and toxicity depend on the amount of exposure, meaning harmless substances can become dangerous in excessive quantities. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h1)

question: What are the two main systems combined within the genito-urinary tract?

options.A: The nervous and skeletal systems
options.B: The digestive and endocrine systems
options.C: The respiratory and circulatory systems
options.D: The urinary and reproductive systems

explanation: The genito-urinary system is a combination of the urinary tract organs and the reproductive organs due to their close developmental and physical links. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T1#GNS213_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why are there 8 pairs of cervical (neck) nerves when there are only 7 cervical vertebrae?

options.A: The eighth nerve originates from the upper thoracic section of the spinal cord
options.B: The cervical spine contains an extra hidden vertebra that houses the eighth nerve
options.C: The first cervical nerve exits above the first vertebra, and the eighth exits below the seventh vertebra
options.D: Cervical nerves divide into two branches as they leave the spinal cord

explanation: Don't let this trick you! Because the first seven nerves exit above their matching vertebrae, an extra eighth nerve sneaks out below the seventh vertebra to bridge us into the chest area. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h1)

question: What is the primary design feature of a Shakir tape used in child health?

options.A: It has built-in electronic Bluetooth sensors
options.B: It uses color-coded zones to screen for malnutrition
options.C: It is made of stretchy elastic for comfortable fitting
options.D: It measures body height instead of limb circumference

explanation: Shakir tapes use red, yellow, and green zones so healthcare workers can instantly spot wasting and malnutrition. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T9#GNS225_U2_T9_h2)

question: Why do doctors evaluate fertility after just six months for women aged thirty-five and older?

options.A: The uterine lining becomes too thick for implantation over time
options.B: Ovarian reserve and egg quality naturally decrease faster at this age
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives take longer to leave the body after age thirty-five
options.D: Older women have a higher rate of chronic pelvic infections

explanation: A quicker evaluation is helpful because a woman's egg quality and supply naturally start to decline faster in her late thirties. Keep up the good work!

question: When should you perform abdominal thrusts on a choking victim?

options.A: When the victim complains of a sore throat
options.B: When the victim cannot speak, cough, or breathe
options.C: When the victim feels a mild tickle in the throat
options.D: When the victim is coughing forcefully and loudly

explanation: If they can cough loudly, encourage them to keep coughing! Reserve abdominal thrusts for severe blockages where they cannot speak, cough, or breathe.

question: A patient is admitted to the ward with severe dehydration and a dry, cracked tongue. What primary mechanical function of the tongue is most likely impaired?

options.A: Directly absorbing simple sugars directly through the taste buds
options.B: Moving and shaping food into a smooth bolus for swallowing
options.C: Filtering dust particles away from the lower respiratory airway
options.D: Producing the primary digestive enzymes needed for starch breakdown

explanation: Dehydration affects oral tissues, making it hard for the tongue to move and moisten food properly into a smooth bolus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary job of the Dorsal Respiratory Group in the medulla?

options.A: Triggering active exhalation during heavy exercise
options.B: Driving the basic automatic rhythm of inhalation
options.C: Controlling voluntary speech patterns during breathing
options.D: Detecting blood oxygen levels directly in the lungs

explanation: The dorsal respiratory group acts as the natural pacemaker for normal, quiet breathing so you don't have to think about every breath.

question: Why do physiological alterations in reproductive health often cause psychological distress for patients?

options.A: Medical protocols mandate strict psychiatric evaluations for all cases
options.B: Physical pain prevents patients from communicating with healthcare providers
options.C: Hormonal imbalances directly destroy brain tissue that regulates mood
options.D: Patients worry about fertility, body image, and societal expectations

explanation: Reproductive health is deeply tied to self-identity, cultural expectations, and family planning goals, making disruptions emotionally heavy. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary benefit of pre-conception genetic screening?

options.A: It allows couples to know their carrier status before pregnancy
options.B: It replaces the need for standard antenatal care
options.C: It immediately cures any existing genetic mutations
options.D: It guarantees that a child will never fall sick

explanation: Pre-conception screening reveals if partners carry matching recessive genes, helping them make informed family planning decisions. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h4)

question: Multi-Drug Resistant TB (MDR-TB) means the bacteria are resistant to which two key drugs?

options.A: Isoniazid and Rifampicin
options.B: Ethambutol and Pyrazinamide
options.C: Streptomycin and Amikacin
options.D: Levofloxacin and Bedaquiline

explanation: MDR-TB specifically means the two heavy-hitters of first-line treatment—isoniazid and rifampicin—no longer work against the strain.

question: Which laboratory test results should a nurse check first to see how well a patient's kidneys are clearing drugs?

options.A: White blood cell count and platelets
options.B: Liver enzymes and serum albumin
options.C: Serum creatinine and BUN (Blood Urea Nitrogen)
options.D: Sodium and potassium electrolytes

explanation: Serum creatinine and BUN are your go-to lab values in the ward for checking how well the kidneys are filtering waste and clearing out medications.

question: Why should you wait for a Nelson inhaler to cool down before trying to wash it?

options.A: To ensure the plastic cork expands to its maximum size
options.B: To save electricity in the utility room
options.C: To let the medication completely dry into a hard solid crust
options.D: To prevent hand burns and avoid cracking the ceramic from sudden temperature changes

explanation: Spot on! Letting it cool protects your hands from burns and stops cold tap water from cracking the hot ceramic jar due to sudden thermal shock.

question: Which muscle tissue type is under voluntary control?

options.A: Skeletal muscle
options.B: Visceral muscle
options.C: Cardiac muscle
options.D: Smooth muscle

explanation: Skeletal muscles attach to bones and allow conscious, voluntary control over body movements. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h1)

question: What is the legal status of treating medical complications from an abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: It is strictly forbidden unless authorized by a high court judge
options.B: It is a legal and medically necessary life-saving intervention
options.C: It is classified as an elective cosmetic procedure
options.D: It is only permitted in federal tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Saving a patient's life by treating emergency complications is always legal and always the top priority in healthcare.

question: What is a key physical difference between a caput succedaneum and a cephalhematoma?

options.A: Cephalhematoma occurs outside the scalp, while caput is inside the brain
options.B: Cephalhematoma always requires immediate surgery, but caput never does
options.C: Caput succedaneum contains pure blood, while cephalhematoma contains serous fluid
options.D: Caput succedaneum crosses suture lines, but a cephalhematoma does not

explanation: Because cephalhematoma is confined beneath the periosteum, it stops strictly at the bone suture lines, whereas caput swelling crosses them freely. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h3)

question: How should a nurse manager figure out how many safety boxes to order for next month?

options.A: By doubling the number of expired items thrown away last year
options.B: By matching the exact number of doctors on duty
options.C: Based on past patient use and expected service volume
options.D: By guessing a random number that fits on the form

explanation: Spot on! Smart ordering looks at past consumption trends and expected patient numbers so you don't overstock or run short.

question: As a nurse, what is your very first priority when a patient arrives with post-abortion complications?

options.A: Conducting a detailed interview about contraception history
options.B: Reporting the incident immediately to law enforcement
options.C: Asking about her religious and cultural beliefs
options.D: Evaluating airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: Safety first! Emergency nursing always starts with the ABCs to stabilize vital signs and catch shock or heavy bleeding early.

question: What's the main thing to know about a disease carrier?

options.A: They only catch infections from dirty soil
options.B: They always have a very high, dangerous fever
options.C: They carry and spread germs without looking or feeling sick
options.D: They completely refuse to take any medications

explanation: Carriers can trick us because they look totally healthy, but they still carry and pass around the infection.

question: Why is it a good idea for a nurse to spend part of a teen's visit talking to them alone?

options.A: To prevent the teenager from asking medical questions
options.B: To save time during a busy hospital shift
options.C: To encourage honest answers about sensitive topics like sex and drugs
options.D: To prove to the parents that they are no longer needed in the room

explanation: Spot on! Teens open up much more honestly about sensitive topics when they know their parents aren't sitting right there listening.

question: A mum has strong contractions, but her cervical dilation hasn't changed at all for three hours. What is this called?

options.A: Arrest of dilatation
options.B: Protracted latent phase
options.C: Precipitous delivery
options.D: Normal descent

explanation: Exactly right. When dilation completely halts for two hours or more during active labour, we call it an arrest of dilatation.

question: What happens if you accidentally use cold water to flush a patient's ear?

options.A: The earwax will instantly dissolve into liquid
options.B: The eardrum will automatically seal itself tighter
options.C: The patient may feel very dizzy and start vomiting
options.D: The water flow will stop completely

explanation: Cold water messes with the balance organs in the inner ear, triggering heavy dizziness and nausea (vertigo). Keep it warm!

question: How does regular physical activity benefit a patient with Type 2 diabetes?

options.A: It helps body cells respond better to available insulin
options.B: It allows the patient to eat unlimited amounts of sugar
options.C: It permanently repairs destroyed cells inside the pancreas
options.D: It replaces the daily need for checking blood sugar levels

explanation: Exercise makes muscle and tissue cells more sensitive to insulin, allowing glucose to move out of the blood and into cells more easily. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h5)

question: What usually happens on the ward when a nurse struggles with poor time management?

options.A: Decreased physical fatigue among nursing staff
options.B: Higher patient satisfaction scores across the unit
options.C: Increased risk of missed care and medication errors
options.D: More time available for professional development

explanation: True! When things get too rushed and we lose control of our time, important tasks or meds can easily slip through the cracks. Take a breath—learning how to pace yourself helps prevent this!

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks gestation arrives with vaginal bleeding and a rigid, painful abdomen. What is the most appropriate immediate nursing action?

options.A: Prepare the patient for an immediate routine digital cervical exam
options.B: Apply warm compresses to the lower abdomen to relieve muscle cramps
options.C: Encourage the patient to walk around to help stimulate labor progress
options.D: Notify the doctor, check vital signs, and monitor fetal heart tones

explanation: An unstable patient presenting with signs of abruption requires immediate medical notification, vital sign stabilization, and fetal surveillance while avoiding internal exams. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h5)

question: When you are cleaning a wound, what is the safest direction to wipe?

options.A: From the outer edges inward to the center
options.B: From the cleanest area to the dirtiest area
options.C: In a wild circular motion all over the skin
options.D: From the bottom of the wound straight up

explanation: Always move from clean to dirty! This golden rule stops you from dragging germs from the surrounding skin right back into the open wound.

question: How does adrenaline directly affect blood flow to the uterus when a mum is stressed?

options.A: It stops all electrical activity in the myometrium instantly
options.B: It dilates blood vessels to increase oxygen delivery to the fetus
options.C: It converts glucose into amniotic fluid rapidly
options.D: It constricts blood vessels and reduces blood flow to the uterus

explanation: Stress hormones cause blood vessels to tighten up (vasoconstriction), drawing blood away from the womb and sending it to the big muscles instead.

question: Why is it so important to counsel patients on what to expect physically before they take abortion medications at home?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of the hospital visit.
options.B: It legally waives the clinic from malpractice claims.
options.C: It prepares them for the expected severe cramps and heavy bleeding at home.
options.D: It prevents heavy bleeding from starting too early.

explanation: Exactly! Knowing what normal cramps and bleeding look like helps patients manage their symptoms calmly at home without unnecessary panic.

question: What is a major public health win when family planning services improve across Nigeria?

options.A: Reducing maternal and infant mortality rates
options.B: Guaranteed economic wealth for every household
options.C: Eliminating all infectious diseases in children
options.D: Removing the need for primary health care clinics

explanation: Proper birth spacing gives mothers and babies a fighting chance at better health, directly lowering maternal and infant deaths. Beautiful impact of nursing care!

question: In nursing research, what do we mean by the word 'population'?

options.A: Every person living in the city where the study takes place
options.B: The specific patients who dropped out of a clinical trial
options.C: The entire group of people the researcher wants to study
options.D: Only the nurses working in a specific hospital ward

explanation: You've got this! In research, the 'population' is just the big group of people you are curious about and want to learn more from. Think of it as the big picture before you zoom in.

question: Where do most unsafe abortions and related complications happen around the world?

options.A: In nations where abortion is completely legal on request
options.B: In urban centers with universal healthcare access
options.C: In low- and middle-income countries with restrictive laws
options.D: In countries with high ratios of trained obstetricians

explanation: Spot on! Strict laws paired with weak healthcare systems in developing regions create a high burden of unsafe procedures. Understanding this helps us advocate for better maternal care.

question: Why is the 'typical use' failure rate for condoms higher than the 'perfect use' rate?

options.A: Incompatible blood types between partners
options.B: User errors like inconsistent use or breakage
options.C: Manufacturing defects in the factory
options.D: Natural expiration of latex while in the box

explanation: Spot on! In the real world, mistakes happen—like not wearing it every time or putting it on late—which lowers effectiveness compared to lab tests.

question: Which high-touch surface in a patient room requires frequent routine disinfection?

options.A: Bedside tables and bed rails
options.B: The inside of closed closet drawers
options.C: Carpeted flooring under the bed
options.D: The ceiling tiles above the bed

explanation: High-touch items like bed rails and tables are frequently contaminated by hands and require regular cleaning. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: What do we call those tiny, pinpoint red or purple spots caused by tiny bleeding vessels under the skin?

options.A: Petechiae
options.B: Pustules
options.C: Macules
options.D: Vesicles

explanation: Petechiae are those little pinpoint spots that show up when tiny blood vessels (capillaries) leak a bit of blood.

question: What is the main focus of a nurse's day-to-day role in neurological care?

options.A: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders independently
options.B: Performing complex brain surgery in the theater
options.C: Prescribing long-term neurological medications
options.D: Protecting delicate brain and nerve tissue from further damage

explanation: You are on the front lines! Nurses play a vital role in preventing nervous system damage and protecting neural tissue before any permanent harm can happen.

question: What does 'anticipatory grief' mean?

options.A: Grief that happens before an expected loss actually occurs
options.B: Grief that completely resolves within twenty-four hours
options.C: Mourning that only affects family members rather than patients
options.D: A sudden emotional breakdown with no clear identifiable trigger

explanation: You've got this! Anticipatory grief simply means processing a loss before it happens, like when someone is facing a long terminal illness. It's totally natural.

question: Why is training community stakeholders so important for health programs?

options.A: It generates financial profit for local hospitals
options.B: It allows them to prescribe pharmaceutical drugs independently
options.C: It turns them into active advocates who champion the cause
options.D: It replaces the need for community health extension workers

explanation: Training empowers leaders with knowledge so they can guide their people and sustain the health program locally. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h4)

question: According to the Swiss Cheese Model, what usually causes patient harm?

options.A: A combination of multiple small system failures
options.B: Unavoidable natural deterioration of medical tools
options.C: Sudden refusal of treatment by the patient's family
options.D: Intentional sabotage by a single disgruntled worker

explanation: Errors usually happen when several safety checks fail all at the same time, letting a mistake reach the patient.

question: What is the main goal of secondary prevention in endocrine and metabolic disorders?

options.A: Providing end-of-life palliative comfort
options.B: Preventing the initial onset of the disease
options.C: Catching early signs through regular screening
options.D: Reversing long-standing organ damage

explanation: Spot-on! Secondary prevention is all about catching hidden problems early through screening tests before they become severe. You've got this!

question: How do patriarchal power structures contribute to the continuation of harmful traditional practices?

options.A: By training nurses to perform traditional surgeries safely
options.B: By providing financial grants to families who follow customs
options.C: By removing laws that protect children from abuse
options.D: By enforcing rules that control female sexuality and behavior

explanation: Societies governed strictly by male-dominated norms often use traditional practices to police women's bodies and ensure submission. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h2)

question: How does keeping a patient close to your body help protect your back during a transfer?

options.A: It reduces the physical load and leverage on your spine
options.B: It makes the patient feel much safer and calmer
options.C: It prevents the patient from falling forward
options.D: It allows you to finish the hospital shift faster

explanation: Keeping heavy objects close to your center of gravity decreases the strain placed on your lower back muscles. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h3)

question: Why is the parasympathetic nervous system referred to as the craniosacral division?

options.A: Its preganglionic fibers originate only in the thoracic spine
options.B: Its nerves emerge from the brain and sacral spinal cord
options.C: Its main neurotransmitter is released in the cranial vault
options.D: Its ganglia are found exclusively in the skull bones

explanation: The craniosacral name reflects the origin of parasympathetic fibers in the brain (cranial) and the sacral segments of the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h5)

question: What main fuel do brain cells (neurons) need constantly to keep working hard?

options.A: Glucose and oxygen
options.B: Fatty acids and glycerol
options.C: Lactic acid and sodium
options.D: Proteins and amino acids

explanation: Neurons are very busy cells! They rely heavily on a continuous supply of glucose and oxygen to keep their energy up and function properly.

question: If a family suddenly loses income due to a job loss, what dietary change is most likely to happen first?

options.A: Stopping all food consumption completely for several days.
options.B: Switching entirely to imported gourmet food items.
options.C: Replacing expensive protein sources and fresh fruits with cheaper, starchy foods.
options.D: Growing all their own wheat and livestock in a small backyard.

explanation: Well done! When cash gets tight, families usually stretch their budget by swapping pricey proteins and fruits for filling, affordable starches.

question: Why are the normal bacteria living inside your large intestine so important?

options.A: They prevent all types of bacterial infections
options.B: They synthesize essential vitamins like vitamin K
options.C: They break down proteins into amino acids
options.D: They line the colon wall to protect against acid

explanation: You got it! Our friendly gut bacteria ferment leftover food and help produce important nutrients like vitamin K, which is essential for blood clotting.

question: Which task is usually handled by the circulating nurse?

options.A: Scrubbing up and handing instruments to the surgeon
options.B: Performing the actual surgical incision on the patient
options.C: Managing the patient's airway and breathing tubes
options.D: Opening sterile packages and managing room equipment

explanation: The circulating nurse is unsterile and moves freely around the room to open supplies, manage equipment, and help the team with whatever they need.

question: When we classify a joint by its 'function', what are we actually describing?

options.A: How much movement the joint allows
options.B: The chemical makeup of its fluid
options.C: The muscles attached to it
options.D: How fast it heals after an injury

explanation: Exactly! Functional classification is simply about range of motion—whether the joint moves freely, a little bit, or not at all.

question: Why does money collected from selling drugs in a DRF go right back into the fund instead of a general government account?

options.A: To ensure the money is immediately available to buy more drug stock
options.B: To pay off international government debts and loans
options.C: To cover the cost of unrelated building construction projects
options.D: To pay the personal salaries of the hospital management team

explanation: You got it! Keeping the money right where it is (ring-fencing it) ensures the pharmacy can restock quickly without waiting for government bureaucracy.

question: What is the main difference between delirium and dementia?

options.A: Delirium is an acute, fluctuating change in mental status
options.B: Dementia can be completely cured with antibiotics
options.C: Dementia causes sudden hallucinations without memory loss
options.D: Delirium develops gradually over several years

explanation: Spot on! Delirium comes on suddenly (often because of an infection or illness) and changes throughout the day. Dementia is a slow, long-term decline in memory and thinking.

question: Why does cigarette smoking increase a woman's chance of getting cervical cancer?

options.A: Tobacco smoke alters systemic blood pressure in the pelvic organs
options.B: Byproducts in tobacco smoke weaken local immunity and damage cervical cells
options.C: Smoking causes immediate permanent closure of the internal cervical os
options.D: Nicotine directly destroys all protective antibodies inside the uterus

explanation: Think of cigarette smoke as carrying harmful chemicals that settle in cervical mucus, wearing down local defenses and damaging cell DNA.

question: Which organ stores and concentrates bile before releasing it?

options.A: Duodenum
options.B: Pancreas
options.C: Gallbladder
options.D: Spleen

explanation: The liver makes the bile, but the gallbladder acts like a storage tank, holding onto it until you eat something fatty.

question: Why do your glands (lymph nodes) often swell up and feel tender when you have an infection?

options.A: The flow of lymph fluid has stopped completely due to local blockage
options.B: White blood cells are rapidly multiplying inside them to fight the invader
options.C: Red blood cells are accumulating in the tissue to repair damaged vessels
options.D: The local temperature has dropped below normal physiological levels

explanation: You got it! When germs are around, your white blood cells throw a massive training and multiplying party inside the nodes, making them temporarily swollen and tender.

question: What does a high dependency ratio mean for a country?

options.A: Every citizen is completely financially independent.
options.B: The government has excess funds for infrastructure projects.
options.C: A small working-age population must support a large number of dependents.
options.D: There are more elderly people than working adults.

explanation: A high dependency ratio means fewer working adults are carrying the financial weight of supporting a large group of children and elderly dependents.

question: What are the two most common major causes of antepartum haemorrhage?

options.A: Ectopic pregnancy and bloody show
options.B: Placenta praevia and abruptio placentae
options.C: Uterine rupture and cervical polyps
options.D: Vasa praevia and gestational diabetes

explanation: Placenta praevia and abruptio placentae are responsible for the vast majority of heavy bleeding episodes in the late stages of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h2)

question: What is usually the first imaging test doctors use to find a heart tumour?

options.A: Routine chest X-ray
options.B: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Echocardiogram

explanation: An echo uses sound waves to let us safely peek inside the heart chambers. It's quick, painless, and the go-to tool for spotting masses. Brilliant nursing insight!

question: What is the main reason to teach an osteoarthritis patient about 'activity pacing'?

options.A: To ensure the patient finishes all chores before morning stiffness starts
options.B: To eliminate all physical movement from their daily routine
options.C: To balance rest periods with tasks and protect joints from overuse
options.D: To prevent the need for any future medical evaluations

explanation: Correct! Pacing helps patients get their daily tasks done without pushing their joints too hard and causing extra pain.

question: Through which bony structure do olfactory nerve fibers pass to reach the brain's olfactory bulb?

options.A: Squamous part of the temporal bone
options.B: Cribriform plate of the ethmoid bone
options.C: Maxillary alveolar process
options.D: Perpendicular plate of the vomer

explanation: Olfactory nerve bundles pass upward through the tiny perforations of the cribriform plate to reach the olfactory bulbs inside the cranium. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h6)

question: What do we call a tumor that has traveled to the brain from another part of the body, like the lungs?

options.A: Benign tumor
options.B: Primary tumor
options.C: Metastatic tumor
options.D: Congenital tumor

explanation: You've got this! When cancer cells break away from a spot like the breast or lungs and travel to the brain, we call it a metastatic (or secondary) tumor. Think of it as a traveler from another part of the body.

question: What goes wrong in the body to cause the symptoms of multiple sclerosis (MS)?

options.A: Accumulation of beta-amyloid plaques in the temporal lobes
options.B: Excessive release of glutamate causing immediate excitotoxicity
options.C: Thrombus formation blocking blood flow in the middle cerebral artery
options.D: Autoimmune destruction of central nervous system myelin

explanation: In MS, the body's immune system mistakenly attacks and strips away the protective myelin coating on nerve fibers, slowing down signals.

question: How does assisted living differ fundamentally from traditional skilled nursing homes?

options.A: It provides a homelike environment that emphasizes autonomy and help with daily tasks rather than heavy medical care
options.B: It relies entirely on family members to provide all professional nursing services
options.C: It refuses admission to any older adult who has a chronic medical condition
options.D: It operates strictly as a hospital ward for patients requiring mechanical ventilation

explanation: Assisted living is meant for folks who just need a little boost with daily activities (like bathing or dressing) but don't need round-the-clock intensive medical nursing.

question: What is the primary effect when significant others view healthcare strictly as a response to severe illness rather than prevention?

options.A: The family will spend excess money on elective wellness check-ups.
options.B: The adolescent will develop an obsession with personal fitness.
options.C: The teenager will independently schedule weekly preventative labs.
options.D: The adolescent will likely skip routine screenings and health checks.

explanation: Household health attitudes shape personal habits; if wellness visits are ignored by family, teenagers rarely seek them out alone. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of community-wide vaccination programs?

options.A: To build herd immunity and protect vulnerable populations
options.B: To replace the need for handwashing and environmental sanitation
options.C: To cure individuals who are already experiencing severe symptoms
options.D: To completely eliminate all bacteria living inside the human gut

explanation: High immunization coverage creates a protective barrier of immune individuals, stopping the spread of disease to those who cannot be vaccinated. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which important nutrient should you encourage in the diet of a patient with heavy periods?

options.A: Iron
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Sodium

explanation: Losing a lot of blood means losing iron, which can lead to tiredness and anemia. Pushing iron-rich foods is a classic nursing intervention!

question: Why are growth hormone and thyroid hormones so critical during infancy and childhood?

options.A: They regulate daily blood sugar levels after meals
options.B: They maintain normal calcium balance in the bones
options.C: They control the immediate fight-or-flight stress reaction
options.D: They coordinate normal skeletal growth and brain maturation

explanation: These two hormones work hand in hand to make sure a child's bones grow properly and their nervous system develops the way it should.

question: A nurse accidentally touches a patient's eyelid with the tip of an eye drop bottle. What is the safest action to take?

options.A: Wipe the tip with a dry tissue and keep using it
options.B: Discard the bottle to prevent spreading infection
options.C: Rinse the bottle tip under hot tap water
options.D: Store the bottle in the refrigerator for twenty-four hours

explanation: Once a dropper tip touches a patient, it is considered contaminated and should not be used again to avoid infection. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why must nurses encourage frequent feeding for a newborn undergoing treatment for jaundice?

options.A: Sucking on the breast helps strengthen the neck muscles against stiffness
options.B: Feeding provides extra calories to help the liver produce more red blood cells
options.C: Milk intake cools the digestive tract and prevents stomach irritation from lights
options.D: Regular feeds promote bowel movements, which help clear bilirubin out of the body

explanation: Frequent feeds mean regular bowel movements, and that is the main way the baby's body passes out the broken-down bilirubin. Feedings are treatment too!

question: Why is it dangerous for a nurse to show judgment or anger toward a patient with abortion complications?

options.A: It legally terminates the nurse's professional employment contract
options.B: It discourages the patient from speaking honestly about what substances were used
options.C: It permanently cures the underlying infection causing the sepsis
options.D: It forces the hospital to close down its emergency department

explanation: Spot on! When patients are afraid of being judged, they hide vital secrets, making it much harder for you to save their lives.

question: Why is pricing drugs based on old historical costs dangerous during high inflation?

options.A: The money collected from sales will be far too little to buy replacement stock
options.B: Patients will refuse to buy the medications because they are too expensive
options.C: Suppliers will refuse to deliver new shipments to the warehouse
options.D: The government will fine the facility for charging below market rates

explanation: During inflation, old prices lose their power! If you sell drugs based on what you paid months ago, your cash won't stretch far enough to buy the new, higher-priced wholesale shipments.

question: When you gently tap and feel a patient's arm to find a good vein, what should a healthy peripheral vein feel like?

options.A: A hard, rigid cord that does not bounce back
options.B: A soft, bouncy vessel that refills after being pressed
options.C: A deep vessel that cannot be felt but looks dark blue
options.D: A pulsing vessel that moves strongly under the finger

explanation: Spot on! Healthy veins feel spongy, elastic, and refill promptly with blood after you press them. You'll get great at spotting these on the ward!

question: Which supporting cells wrap around brain capillaries to help form the blood-brain barrier?

options.A: Schwann cells
options.B: Ependymal cells
options.C: Microglia
options.D: Astrocytes

explanation: Astrocytes are star-shaped glial cells that put out little 'feet' to wrap around blood vessels and protect brain tissue.

question: Which of the following is an effective way to help prevent puerperal sepsis during labor?

options.A: Delaying bladder emptying until after delivery
options.B: Encouraging strict bed rest for the entire duration of labor
options.C: Limiting the number of unnecessary vaginal examinations
options.D: Avoiding all routine perineal hygiene measures

explanation: Every vaginal exam is a chance to introduce bacteria. Doing only necessary exams helps keep the birth canal safer from outside germs.

question: You want to know how a newly admitted patient is coping emotionally with a sickle cell crisis. What is the best way to ask?

options.A: Wait until the patient brings up mental health issues on their own
options.B: Ask closed yes-or-no questions to speed up your nursing documentation
options.C: Use open-ended questions to invite the patient to share their feelings
options.D: Focus strictly on pain scores and laboratory blood test results

explanation: Open-ended questions like 'How are you holding up today?' give patients the safe space they need to truly open up.

question: A patient develops a bone infection in the foot after stepping on a nail while wearing sneakers. Which organism is most likely involved?

options.A: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
options.B: Salmonella typhi
options.C: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.D: Mycobacterium tuberculosis

explanation: Puncture wounds through rubber-soled shoes, like trainers, commonly introduce Pseudomonas bacteria directly into the foot bones. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h2)

question: When should active teenagers drink water during sports or exercise?

options.A: Only when they feel a strong sense of thirst
options.B: Regularly throughout the day and during activity, before feeling thirsty
options.C: Only during meal times with solid food
options.D: Exclusively after finishing all sports or exercises

explanation: Good to know! Thirst usually means the body is already slightly dehydrated, so it's best to sip water steadily before feeling extremely thirsty.

question: Why can it be dangerous to combine an expectorant with a cough suppressant?

options.A: It can trap thinned mucus in the airways if the patient cannot cough
options.B: It leads to severe kidney failure within twenty-four hours
options.C: It completely neutralizes the chemical structure of both drugs
options.D: It causes an immediate and dangerous drop in the patient's heart rate

explanation: Think about it: if the drug turns the mucus watery but you stop the patient from coughing, that fluid gets trapped and blocks their airway. Dangerous combo!

question: Why is healthy, unbroken skin considered part of the innate immune system?

options.A: It contains mature T-lymphocytes that destroy foreign organisms
options.B: It acts as a physical barrier that stops pathogens from entering the body
options.C: It actively manufactures specific antibodies against local skin bacteria
options.D: It produces high levels of inflammatory cytokines during minor scrapes

explanation: Spot on! Your skin is your body's first wall of defense, stopping germs from getting inside in the first place.

question: Which hormone relaxes the muscles of the urinary tract during pregnancy, causing the ureters to widen?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body. During pregnancy, this causes the tubes carrying urine from the kidneys to widen. You've got this!

question: What does informed consent require before a client receives a contraceptive method?

options.A: Proof of employment and stable monthly income
options.B: A written letter of approval from a community chief
options.C: Complete agreement from the client's extended family
options.D: Full understanding of benefits, risks, and correct usage

explanation: Informed consent means the client knows what to expect, including how the method works and its potential side effects, before they choose it. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h4)

question: An older adult has weak muscles and is getting ready to leave the hospital. What is the most important step to prevent falls?

options.A: Removing all windows from the patient's home environment
options.B: Ensuring the patient has proper instruction in using an assistive device
options.C: Restricting the patient to bed rest to prevent any movement
options.D: Encouraging the patient to walk barefoot indoors for better grip

explanation: Walking aids like canes or walkers only work if the patient knows how to use them safely and confidently!

question: A patient with diabetes looks shaky, dizzy, and is sweating before lunch. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Administer the scheduled dose of daily long-acting insulin
options.B: Send a blood sample to the laboratory for an HbA1c test
options.C: Encourage the patient to sleep until the symptoms pass
options.D: Check blood glucose levels and prepare a fast-acting carbohydrate

explanation: Shakiness and sweating are red flags for low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Always check the blood glucose first and have a fast sugar source ready! Patient safety comes first.

question: What is a major difference between paracetamol (acetaminophen) and NSAIDs?

options.A: Acetaminophen causes significant gastric bleeding
options.B: NSAIDs work exclusively inside the spinal cord
options.C: NSAIDs have no effect on body temperature
options.D: Acetaminophen lacks peripheral anti-inflammatory action

explanation: Both lower fever and ease pain, but paracetamol doesn't fight body inflammation or affect bleeding the way NSAIDs do.

question: What does decentralized decision-making mean in primary nursing?

options.A: Authority for clinical choices rests directly with the bedside nurse.
options.B: Nurse managers handle every single choice regarding patient hygiene.
options.C: All hospital decisions must be approved by the chief medical director.
options.D: Patients make all of their own medical treatment decisions alone.

explanation: Decentralized just means power is shared! The nurse right there at the bedside has the backing to make immediate, smart clinical choices for their patient.

question: How does the daily objective of a public health nurse differ from that of a bedside hospital nurse?

options.A: The public health nurse focuses on disease prevention for populations, while the bedside nurse focuses on acute care for individuals
options.B: The public health nurse diagnoses surgical conditions, while the bedside nurse only administers oral medications
options.C: The public health nurse works exclusively with doctors, while the bedside nurse works completely alone
options.D: The public health nurse ignores chronic illnesses, while the bedside nurse only handles emergency trauma

explanation: The core distinction lies in the population-wide prevention mindset of public health versus the individual-focused healing mindset of clinical care. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h4)

question: A patient just had cataract surgery and is getting ready to go home. What is a key instruction to give them?

options.A: Wash your face vigorously with antibacterial soap daily
options.B: Sleep flat on your back without using any pillows
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and straining during bowel movements
options.D: Keep the affected eye uncovered at all times

explanation: Spot on! Straining or heavy lifting ramps up the pressure inside the eye, which is the last thing you want right after eye surgery.

question: To call leprosy 'paucibacillary', what is the highest number of skin lesions a patient can have?

options.A: Ten lesions
options.B: Twenty lesions
options.C: Five lesions
options.D: Two lesions

explanation: Great job! 'Pauci' means few. Having 5 or fewer skin lesions puts it in the paucibacillary category.

question: How does the hippocampus work when it comes to human memory?

options.A: It acts as the final permanent storage vault for every memory
options.B: It translates what you see into spoken words
options.C: It organizes new memories and helps send them to the cortex
options.D: It deletes sad memories to protect your mental health

explanation: Correct! Think of the hippocampus as a sorting station that processes new memories and helps ship them to the cerebral cortex for permanent storage.

question: Why does a grand multiparous woman have a higher risk of her uterus tearing (rupturing) during labor?

options.A: Her baby is usually much smaller than average.
options.B: Her contractions are always weaker than normal.
options.C: Her pelvic bones widen permanently after the first child is born.
options.D: Her womb muscle has less stretch and may carry old scars.

explanation: Years of stretching, scar tissue from past surgeries, and less elastic muscle mean the womb can struggle to handle strong labor contractions.

question: What does continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber usually mean?

options.A: An air leak in the system
options.B: Normal lung re-expansion
options.C: High suction pressure levels
options.D: Blocked drainage tubing

explanation: Correct! While a little bit of bubbling can be normal, constant bubbling is a red flag that there's an unwanted air leak somewhere in the tubing or connections.

question: Why do doctors urgently order a CT scan of the head for a patient who suddenly becomes unconscious?

options.A: To quickly spot bleeding, blood clots, or structural brain damage
options.B: To measure the exact electrical activity firing across the cortex
options.C: To check for bacterial growth within the cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: To determine if the patient has ingested specific toxic drugs

explanation: Brilliant! A CT scan gives a fast, clear picture to see if there is dangerous bleeding or a blood clot that needs immediate attention.

question: Why must a nurse use soap and water instead of alcohol gel after caring for a patient with Clostridioides difficile?

options.A: Alcohol rubs do not reliably destroy bacterial spores
options.B: Soap and water dry out the skin much faster
options.C: Spores dissolve instantly when exposed to hand sanitizer
options.D: Alcohol gel leaves a sticky residue on surgical gloves

explanation: Clostridioides difficile produces tough spores that resist alcohol sanitizers, requiring physical washing to rinse them away. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: How do osmotic diuretics like mannitol physically keep water inside the kidney tubes?

options.A: By blocking the hormone aldosterone in the collecting duct
options.B: By chemically binding to all the sodium ions in the filtrate
options.C: By changing the electrical charge of the tubular walls
options.D: By creating a high osmotic pull that keeps water from being reabsorbed

explanation: Because mannitol cannot be reabsorbed by the body, it acts like a sponge in the kidney tubules, holding onto water through osmosis.

question: Which cells in the testes are responsible for producing testosterone?

options.A: Spermatids
options.B: Leydig cells
options.C: Sertoli cells
options.D: Spermatogonia

explanation: Leydig cells are found between the tubules and synthesize the primary male sex hormone, testosterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the easiest and most sensitive way for a nurse to check for early fluid buildup at home?

options.A: Weighing the patient daily at the same time
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the arm
options.C: Asking the patient if they feel thirsty
options.D: Checking shoe size once a week

explanation: Water weighs a lot! A sudden climb on the bathroom scale is almost always the earliest sign that fluid is starting to build up in the body.

question: A patient swallowed a small toy that got stuck in their throat. Why would a doctor perform a laryngoscopy?

options.A: To test the patient's swallowing reflex
options.B: To locate and safely remove the inhaled object
options.C: To measure the oxygen content in the lungs
options.D: To check for chronic bacterial throat infections

explanation: Spot on! When something gets stuck where it shouldn't be, this procedure lets the clinician spot the object and safely take it out.

question: Why is clear paperwork and documentation so important when transferring a patient to a teaching hospital?

options.A: To prove to the hospital management that nurses are working hard
options.B: To increase the hospital billing charges for the patient
options.C: To ensure continuity of care and prevent treatment delays
options.D: To make the patient's folder look bulky and professional

explanation: Good transfer notes give the new team a clear history of what has been done, making sure the patient keeps getting safe, uninterrupted care without repeating tests.

question: Where is the pleural space actually located in the body?

options.A: Between the visceral pleura and the parietal pleura
options.B: Directly inside the chambers of the human heart
options.C: Between the skin and the outer rib cage muscles
options.D: Inside the main bronchial tubes of the lungs

explanation: Spot on! It sits neatly as a tiny space between the two membrane layers that wrap around and protect our lungs.

question: Which key parts of the body work together to control the normal female monthly cycle?

options.A: Thyroid, adrenal glands, and pancreas
options.B: Brain and outer blood vessels
options.C: Hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and ovaries
options.D: Heart and lungs

explanation: You've got this! The hypothalamus, pituitary gland, and ovaries form the main hormonal team (the HPO axis) that drives the female reproductive cycle.

question: Oops! A scrubbed nurse accidentally drops their hands below waist level before putting on a gown. What should they do?

options.A: Ask the circulator to spray antiseptic on the hands
options.B: Lift hands back up and start gowning
options.C: Wipe hands quickly with alcohol rub and keep going
options.D: Treat the hands as contaminated and repeat the entire scrub

explanation: Anything below the waist is considered unsafe territory. Better safe than sorry—time for a quick re-scrub!

question: What is a major contributing factor to caregiver burden in palliative home care?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free time available to family members
options.B: Juggling household duties, financial stress, and nursing care
options.C: Having too many professional nurses visiting the home
options.D: The patient refusing to eat hospital-prepared meals

explanation: Family caregivers often shoulder overwhelming multi-role responsibilities without adequate rest, leading to burnout. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h4)

question: What is a major reason why clients sometimes stop using modern contraceptives early?

options.A: Sudden nationwide shortages of barrier supplies
options.B: Automatic expiration of contraceptive efficacy after one month
options.C: Anxiety and fear regarding normal physiological side effects
options.D: Mandatory government limits on the duration of use

explanation: Spot on! Many clients stop using a method when they notice minor changes like spotting simply because nobody warned them it's a normal body reaction.

question: What is a Type A adverse drug reaction like?

options.A: It is bizarre and unrelated to the drug's normal actions
options.B: It is an allergic response mediated by the immune system
options.C: It is dose-dependent and predictable based on pharmacology
options.D: It only occurs when a patient stops taking a medication

explanation: Spot on! Type A reactions happen because the drug's normal effect is just too strong, usually when the dose is a bit too high for the patient.

question: Which of these means a planned home birth is definitely NOT safe?

options.A: Single fetus in cephalic presentation
options.B: Strong personal desire for home birth
options.C: Previous cesarean section delivery
options.D: Spontaneous onset of labor at term

explanation: Spot on. A uterus with a scar from a past CS has a risk of tearing during labor, so a hospital setting is much safer.

question: Which specific vaccination is especially critical for healthcare workers who handle decontamination and sharps?

options.A: Rabies vaccine
options.B: Tetanus toxoid
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Yellow fever

explanation: The Hepatitis B vaccine is essential for protecting staff against bloodborne pathogen exposure from contaminated instruments and needles. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which routine test is done at antenatal clinics to screen for gestational diabetes or kidney issues?

options.A: Liver biopsy for enzyme levels
options.B: Sputum microscopy for bacteria
options.C: Urinalysis for protein and glucose
options.D: Electrocardiogram for heart rhythm

explanation: Testing urine samples at every visit is a quick way to spot early signs of gestational diabetes or high blood pressure in pregnancy.

question: What does it usually mean if a patient's urea level is very high compared to their creatinine?

options.A: Excessive dietary intake of green leafy vegetables
options.B: Dehydration or reduced blood flow to the kidneys
options.C: An acute infection in the urinary bladder
options.D: Severe damage directly to the kidney tissue

explanation: Great thinking! When blood flow to the kidneys drops (like when someone is severely dehydrated), the body holds onto urea much more than creatinine.

question: Why must the antiseptic skin prep dry completely before the needle enters?

options.A: To prevent the alcohol from destroying the medication
options.B: To cool down the muscle tissue for less pain
options.C: To make the skin slippery so the needle enters smoother
options.D: To allow the antiseptic time to kill microbes and prevent stinging

explanation: Chemical disinfectants need contact time to eliminate surface pathogens, and wet alcohol entering a puncture wound causes sharp pain. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h5)

question: What does a delayed capillary refill time usually indicate about the patient?

options.A: Excessive fluid intake during the day
options.B: Poor peripheral blood circulation
options.C: An infection in the heart valves
options.D: High levels of oxygen in the blood

explanation: When blood flow to the extremities is sluggish, it takes longer for color to return to the nail bed after pressing. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h4)

question: What makes an injection truly safe in healthcare?

options.A: It causes no harm to the patient or healthcare worker
options.B: It costs less than oral medications
options.C: It is performed only by senior doctors
options.D: It is always administered in the gluteal muscle

explanation: Spot on! A safe injection protects everyone—the patient getting treated, you as the healthcare worker, and our community from hazardous waste.

question: Why is brain damage often permanent, unlike injuries in other parts of the body?

options.A: Neurons have a very limited capacity to regenerate once destroyed.
options.B: Neurons reproduce too rapidly for normal cellular repair mechanisms.
options.C: Surrounding glial cells actively prevent any blood flow to the area.
options.D: Neurons store excessive amounts of toxic waste products.

explanation: Unlike skin or muscle tissue, mature brain cells don't easily divide or replace themselves. Once lost, it's very hard for them to grow back.

question: Which group of people is diagnosed with disseminated sclerosis more often?

options.A: Inhabitants of high-altitude deserts
options.B: Children under five
options.C: Elderly men
options.D: Women

explanation: Studies consistently show that disseminated sclerosis affects women about twice as often as men. Good to keep in mind for your exams!

question: Where do water-soluble nutrients go right after crossing the intestinal wall?

options.A: Upward into the lungs to assist with oxygen exchange
options.B: Directly into the urinary bladder for quick disposal
options.C: Into the portal circulation straight to the liver
options.D: Directly to the skin surface for temperature control

explanation: You're doing great! Water-soluble nutrients take a direct trip through the portal vein to the liver, where they get filtered and prepped for the rest of the body.

question: Why must a nurse view pharmacotherapy as a balance between benefits and risks?

options.A: Therapeutic effects only occur when toxic reactions are actively triggered
options.B: Patients will refuse treatment if they know about any potential side effects
options.C: Every medication carries some level of inherent hazard alongside its healing properties
options.D: Hospital policies require reporting all minor medication side effects daily

explanation: All drugs have the potential to cause harm, so nurses must weigh therapeutic gains against possible toxic effects. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h1)

question: A stroke patient is struggling with swallowing food safely and speaking clearly. Who should the nurse call for help?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Social worker
options.C: Prosthetist
options.D: Physiotherapist

explanation: Speech therapists are experts at helping patients overcome both communication hurdles and swallowing issues (dysphagia).

question: Which hormone is secreted by the early trophoblast cells to signal pregnancy?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: hCG is the primary hormone detected in pregnancy tests, produced by the cells that attach to the uterine wall. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h5)

question: A family caring for a child with cerebral palsy is struggling to afford mobility aids and therapy sessions. What kind of support should you recommend?

options.A: Financial assistance and rehabilitation services
options.B: Commercial banking loans
options.C: Adult vocational training centers
options.D: Tax exemption advisory boards

explanation: Welfare grants and rehabilitation therapy are designed to directly help families manage the financial and physical demands of special needs care.

question: Facing discrimination over a long period of time causes which physical response in the body?

options.A: Enhanced muscle growth and physical strength
options.B: Persistent stress and elevated cortisol levels
options.C: Permanent immunity to common infections
options.D: Immediate decrease in blood pressure

explanation: Discrimination acts as a constant stressor, keeping stress hormones like cortisol high and wearing down a person's health over time. Keep learning!

question: In rehabilitation, what do we mean when we talk about setting SMART goals?

options.A: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
options.B: Safe, Medical, Active, Realistic, Team-oriented
options.C: Systematic, Managed, Assessed, Recorded, Tested
options.D: Simple, Meaningful, Accountable, Rapid, Targeted

explanation: SMART goals give patients and the healthcare team clear targets so everyone can see real progress being made day by day.

question: How many blood vessels are normally found in a healthy newborn's umbilical cord?

options.A: Two arteries and one vein
options.B: Two veins and one artery
options.C: Two veins and two arteries
options.D: One vein and one artery

explanation: Think of it as 3 vessels total: 2 smaller arteries taking used blood away from the baby, and 1 bigger vein bringing fresh oxygenated blood back to them.

question: Within how many hours of a possible HIV exposure should Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) be started for the best results?

options.A: Within 72 hours
options.B: Within 1 week
options.C: Within 24 days
options.D: Within 48 weeks

explanation: Time matters! Starting PEP within 72 hours gives the best chance of preventing HIV after an exposure.

question: What is the common underlying problem in chronic brain diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's?

options.A: Acute bacterial infection inside the ventricular system
options.B: Complete destruction of the skull bone structure
options.C: Abnormal folding and accumulation of specific proteins
options.D: Sudden rupture of major cerebral aneurysms

explanation: In these conditions, certain proteins misfold and clump together into sticky clusters that slowly harm brain cells over time.

question: How does the body normally keep its hormone levels balanced and in check?

options.A: Negative feedback loops
options.B: Enzyme degradation
options.C: Positive feedback loops
options.D: Direct neural stimulation

explanation: Think of negative feedback as the body's natural thermostat or brake system. When hormone levels get too high, it signals the body to slow down production so everything stays balanced. You've got this!

question: Why is fast teamwork among healthcare staff so essential when managing GI complications?

options.A: Conditions can deteriorate into life-threatening emergencies very quickly
options.B: Nurses are not allowed to touch patients without a doctor present
options.C: Medical staff must share paperwork equally among themselves
options.D: Collaborative care guarantees that surgery will never be needed

explanation: You got it! Emergencies like bowel tears or massive bleeding move fast, meaning the team has to act together instantly to keep the patient safe. Teamwork makes the dream work in nursing!

question: A patient walks into the clinic with lower tummy pain and unusual discharge. What serious upper-body complication should a nurse watch out for if this is left untreated?

options.A: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Type 2 diabetes mellitus

explanation: If a lower infection is ignored, it can travel upwards into the reproductive organs and trigger pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).
