question: When does most of the myelination (insulation) happen in the human nervous system?

options.A: Only after a person reaches full physical adulthood
options.B: Immediately before the neural tube closes
options.C: Starting late in fetal development and continuing into adolescence
options.D: Exclusively during the first three weeks of embryonic life

explanation: Exactly! Myelination starts before birth for basic tasks, but it keeps going all through childhood and into our teenage years.

question: A patient on a water pill (diuretic) keeps waking up all through the night. Why is this happening?

options.A: The drug stimulates brain activity like caffeine
options.B: The medicine makes the patient urinate frequently
options.C: The medication causes severe joint pain
options.D: The pill induces sudden anxiety attacks

explanation: Diuretics make the kidneys produce more urine. Naturally, this means the patient has to make frequent trips to the restroom at night!

question: How does a female condom stay securely in place inside the vagina?

options.A: A flexible inner ring at the closed end
options.B: Suction created by an external pump
options.C: Sutures placed by a healthcare provider
options.D: An adhesive strip on the outside

explanation: You nailed it! The inner ring at the closed end helps the user push and anchor the pouch securely inside.

question: Why do nurses try to avoid using a urinary catheter unless it's truly necessary?

options.A: It brings a high risk of introducing bacteria into the urinary tract
options.B: It is extremely painful for every patient who receives one
options.C: It requires surgical removal by a urologist
options.D: It permanently weakens the bladder muscles within hours

explanation: You got it! Because catheters bypass the body's natural defenses, they easily let germs in, making infections a big risk. That's why we only use them when we really have to.

question: Which family planning method protects against both pregnancy AND sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal implants
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Barrier methods
options.D: Natural fertility awareness

explanation: Great job! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block physical contact and fluids, giving you dual protection against both STIs and unwanted pregnancy.

question: What is a helpful nursing action to ease a patient's anxiety about being stuck in traction?

options.A: Explain the equipment clearly and keep their call bell close by
options.B: Take away all entertainment to help them sleep
options.C: Promise to take the traction off whenever they get bored
options.D: Tell family members not to visit so the room stays quiet

explanation: You've got this! Knowing how the equipment works and knowing help is just a button press away builds huge trust and comfort for the patient.

question: When is a doctor or lab scientist most likely to order a peripheral blood smear along with a regular full blood count?

options.A: As a quick kidney check before surgery
options.B: To check how much iron the patient eats over time
options.C: When the standard blood count shows unexpected results
options.D: To replace measuring total haemoglobin

explanation: A blood smear lets the lab actually look at the cells under a microscope when the numbers on the regular blood test look a bit strange.

question: Which health history is a strict warning (contraindication) against using estrogen-based birth control?

options.A: Simple tension headaches
options.B: Mild seasonal pollen allergies
options.C: Well-controlled iron deficiency
options.D: History of deep vein thrombosis

explanation: Spot on! Estrogen can raise clotting risks, so giving it to someone with a history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is unsafe. Always check patient history first!

question: During a home visit in a rural village, a nurse has to make important care decisions independently. Which nursing field is this?

options.A: Operating theatre nursing
options.B: Intensive care unit nursing
options.C: Community health nursing
options.D: Central sterile supply nursing

explanation: Exactly! Out in the field, community nurses often work on their own, trusting their training and assessment skills to make great clinical choices.

question: Why is writing down complete notes about pain care so important for nurses?

options.A: It replaces the need to talk directly with the patient.
options.B: It is only required for legal protection during lawsuits.
options.C: It ensures safe continuity of care and evaluates if treatment worked.
options.D: It allows the hospital to bill insurance companies faster.

explanation: Clear notes help the whole healthcare team see what worked, keep the patient safe, and coordinate the next steps smoothly.

question: A nurse is reviewing survey data where patients ranked hospital food from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Which measures can be used?

options.A: Only the arithmetic mean
options.B: Only the range and variance
options.C: Median and mode
options.D: Mean and standard deviation

explanation: Since these are ranked choices, we can find the middle position (median) and the most frequent rank (mode). You're doing great!

question: What is the main use of a urinal in the ward?

options.A: To collect stool samples from patients with gastrointestinal bleeding
options.B: To measure precise fluid intake during intravenous therapy
options.C: To collect urine from male patients who cannot walk to the bathroom
options.D: To replace indwelling urinary catheters in surgical patients permanently

explanation: Urinals are shaped specially for male anatomy so patients who are stuck in bed can pass urine easily without fuss. You will see these all the time on the medical-surgical wards!

question: A nurse notices women in a village prefer risky home births due to tradition. What is the best first step?

options.A: Report all pregnant women in the village to the local police
options.B: Provide culturally sensitive education and build trust regarding hospital delivery benefits
options.C: Refuse to treat any woman who has previously given birth at home
options.D: Ignore the practice since culture cannot be influenced by health workers

explanation: Yarn true! Respecting people's culture while gently building trust is the best way to help them see the safety of hospital deliveries. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why are community referrals and health linkages important in post-abortion care?

options.A: They replace the need for emergency treatment during complications
options.B: They ensure that the patient never has to visit a hospital again
options.C: They support long-term wellness and prevent future reproductive health issues
options.D: They are only used to track legal infractions in the community

explanation: Well done! Community linkages connect patients to ongoing check-ups, STI care, and other vital primary health resources.

question: When we talk about the political dimension of health inclusion, what are we focusing on?

options.A: Requiring all nurses to register and vote for a specific political party
options.B: Ensuring hospitals only open in politically stable urban states
options.C: The ability of citizens to have a voice in decisions and health policies affecting them
options.D: Allowing government ministers to manage daily hospital ward rosters

explanation: Correct! Political inclusion means ordinary people have a say in the health policies and decisions that shape their communities.

question: How do DRF exemptions help protect public health in the wider community?

options.A: By ensuring contagious diseases are treated promptly without financial delay
options.B: By providing government grants to local chemical manufacturing plants
options.C: By lowering the market price of medical equipment for private clinics
options.D: By forcing pharmaceutical companies to lower their manufacturing costs

explanation: Great thinking! Treating infectious illnesses right away stops the disease from spreading further among the general public.

question: When is an antiarrhythmic drug like amiodarone usually given during resuscitation?

options.A: For persistent shockable rhythms like ventricular fibrillation
options.B: As the first medication before any chest compressions begin
options.C: To treat severe sinus bradycardia and low blood pressure
options.D: To reverse respiratory depression caused by opioid overdose

explanation: We pull out amiodarone when electric shocks and CPR haven't quite managed to fix stubborn rhythms like V-fib yet.

question: Why do positive signs give us 100% certainty of pregnancy while probable signs do not?

options.A: Positive signs are caused exclusively by the presence of a developing fetus
options.B: Positive signs are reported directly by the mother based on her daily feelings
options.C: Probable signs can only be seen using expensive hospital laboratory machines
options.D: Probable signs only appear briefly during the final weeks of gestation

explanation: Exactly! Positive signs leave zero room for doubt because nothing else in the human body can create a fetal heartbeat or show a baby on a scan.

question: Why does recovery from an axonotmesis injury take many months to occur?

options.A: Inflammation must completely clear out of the central nervous system before peripheral signals are allowed to pass.
options.B: Specialized white blood cells must first convert the damaged myelin into functional scar tissue.
options.C: The body has to completely rebuild the surrounding bone structure before nerve fibers can begin to cross the gap.
options.D: The regrowing axon must slowly creep down the remaining connective tube at a rate of about one millimeter per day.

explanation: Axonal regeneration is a very slow biological process, requiring months for fibers to travel from the injury site all the way back to muscles in the feet or hands. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h3)

question: When should you ideally start planning for a neurological client's discharge?

options.A: Only after all therapy sessions are finished
options.B: The evening before the client goes home
options.C: When the doctor finally writes the discharge order
options.D: On the day of hospital admission

explanation: It sounds early, but starting day one gives you enough breathing room to sort out equipment, teach family members, and prep the home before discharge day sneaks up!

question: Which of these is the main reproductive organ in females?

options.A: Uterus
options.B: Fallopian tube
options.C: Ovary
options.D: Vagina

explanation: Spot on! The ovaries are the primary organs because they make the eggs and female hormones. The rest are helper structures.

question: Which hormone causes the milk ejection reflex (let-down)?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Correct! Oxytocin is the 'let-down' hormone that makes the milk flow smoothly for your baby.

question: Which part of the Glasgow Coma Scale is usually seen as the best clue to how well a patient will recover?

options.A: Verbal response
options.B: Pupillary reflex
options.C: Motor response
options.D: Eye opening

explanation: The motor response checks deep brain pathways. It gives nurses and doctors the strongest clue about how a patient is recovering after a head injury.

question: Which waste product in a U&E panel comes directly from normal muscle breakdown?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Urea
options.C: Bicarbonate
options.D: Creatinine

explanation: Well done! Creatinine is a natural byproduct of your everyday muscle activity that healthy kidneys filter right out of the blood.

question: Your patient is scheduled for an MRI, but mentions they have a permanent heart pacemaker. What should you do right away?

options.A: Wrap the patient's chest in a lead apron to block the magnetic field
options.B: Administer a mild sedative to calm the patient before the scan starts
options.C: Proceed with the scan because pacemakers are safe inside the magnet
options.D: Notify the ordering physician and the radiology department immediately

explanation: Hold on! That giant magnet can pull on metal implants and ruin a pacemaker. Always flag this to the team immediately to keep the patient safe.

question: What is a very common emotional worry for patients facing a terminal diagnosis?

options.A: Excitement about trying new experimental diets
options.B: Fear of becoming a burden to loved ones
options.C: Desire to return to full-time strenuous employment
options.D: Indifference toward family relationships

explanation: Patients with serious illnesses often carry a heavy heart, worrying about the physical, emotional, and financial strain they might put on their family. Empathy is our greatest tool!

question: What emergency medicine is given right away after a nurse accidentally pricks their finger with an HIV-contaminated needle?

options.A: Broad-spectrum antibiotic coverage
options.B: Antiretroviral maintenance therapy
options.C: Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP)
options.D: Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP)

explanation: PEP is taken promptly after a potential exposure to stop the virus before it takes hold. Stay safe out there!

question: A patient is medically ready to leave the ward, but has no home, money, or family support. Who is best suited to help?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The laboratory scientist
options.C: The medical social worker
options.D: The chief operating surgeon

explanation: Medical social workers are champions at discharge planning! They help find shelter and connect vulnerable patients with community support systems.

question: Why does too much heat around the testes negatively affect a man's fertility?

options.A: It prevents the proper production and movement of sperm
options.B: It destroys the testosterone receptors in the liver
options.C: It stops the prostate gland from making seminal fluid
options.D: It causes an immediate blockage of the urethra

explanation: Correct! Sperm love a cool environment. Too much heat slows them down and stops them from forming properly. Another one in the bag!

question: A rural health clinic has only two nurses on duty. Which staffing approach ensures the best care for the community?

options.A: Firing the nurses and hiring administrative clerks
options.B: Employing polyvalent nurses trained in multiple care areas
options.C: Restricting care strictly to adult male patients
options.D: Closing the clinic until a specialist doctor arrives

explanation: Spot on! Having polyvalent nurses means a small team can safely and confidently handle a wide variety of health needs in the community.

question: What is a dual-chamber pacemaker designed to do?

options.A: Pace both an atrium and a ventricle
options.B: Store two separate batteries for emergencies
options.C: Pace the left and right lungs together
options.D: Monitor blood pressure and breathing rate

explanation: A dual-chamber system uses two leads to coordinate contractions in both upper and lower chambers of the heart. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h2)

question: How would you best describe peristalsis?

options.A: Wave-like muscle contractions that push food forward
options.B: Localized churning that mixes food in the small intestine
options.C: The absorption of water through the large bowel wall
options.D: The secretion of digestive enzymes by the pancreas

explanation: Spot on! Think of peristalsis like a wave of muscle squeezes moving food steadily along down the digestive tube.

question: What is the typical safe suction pressure range for an adult patient?

options.A: 500 to 600 mmHg
options.B: 10 to 20 mmHg
options.C: 80 to 120 mmHg
options.D: 200 to 300 mmHg

explanation: Pressures between 80 and 120 mmHg are strong enough to remove thick mucus without causing excessive trauma to the airway lining. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which management theory focuses the most on efficiency, timing tasks, and standard work routines?

options.A: Human Relations Theory
options.B: Democratic Leadership Theory
options.C: Chaos Management Theory
options.D: Scientific Management

explanation: Scientific management looks closely at how tasks are done to cut out wasted time and make every action as efficient as possible.

question: What is the job of a cerumenolytic drug like carbamide peroxide?

options.A: To numb the ear canal before minor procedures
options.B: To kill bacteria causing deep ear infections
options.C: To soften and break down hard earwax for easy removal
options.D: To dry up fluid draining from the eardrum

explanation: Cerumenolytics do exactly what their name suggests: they break down stubborn, impacted earwax so it's a breeze to clear out of the canal.

question: What is a major cause of faecal incontinence among women in many resource-limited settings?

options.A: Obstetric trauma during childbirth
options.B: Weakness of the upper arm muscles
options.C: Excessive daily consumption of citrus fruits
options.D: Chronic overuse of inhaled medications

explanation: Difficult deliveries with untreated or poorly repaired perineal tears are a leading cause of sphincter damage and subsequent incontinence in women. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h3)

question: Where does primary-level rehabilitation usually happen?

options.A: In high-tech national trauma centers
options.B: At large university teaching hospitals only
options.C: At local health posts and primary health centers
options.D: Inside specialized tertiary surgical wards

explanation: That's right! Primary-level care is the closest healthcare point to the community, handling basic checks and early support right where people live.

question: In livestock farming, what do we call a disease that can jump between animals and humans?

options.A: A plant infection caused by heavy rainfall
options.B: A mechanical failure of milking equipment
options.C: An illness that can spread between animals and humans
options.D: A vitamin deficiency found only in farm workers

explanation: Zoonotic diseases are infections that naturally pass from animals to us. Think of illnesses like bird flu or rabies!

question: When assessing a patient who might easily catch infections, what should a nurse check?

options.A: Reviewing vaccination records and living conditions
options.B: Manufacturing new vaccines in the laboratory
options.C: Performing surgical operations to remove pathogens
options.D: Prescribing prophylactic antibiotics independently

explanation: You're thinking like a nurse! Checking immunization history and home surroundings helps us understand a patient's risk level.

question: How can you best protect a patient's dignity and privacy when giving them a bed bath?

options.A: By keeping completely silent so they don't feel awkward
options.B: By asking all family members to stay outside forever
options.C: By opening the ward windows wide for fresh air
options.D: By keeping the patient covered with a sheet and exposing only the area being washed

explanation: Brilliant! Strategic draping with a bedsheet keeps your patient covered, warm, and feeling respected while you work.

question: In community health, why can't just one type of health worker solve every problem?

options.A: Government policies forbid single-worker clinics
options.B: Doctors lack the training to visit local neighborhoods
options.C: Nurses refuse to handle community cases on their own
options.D: Community issues involve physical, social, and economic factors

explanation: Spot on! Because a patient's health is tied to housing, money, and food, we need a mix of specialists to truly help.

question: Why is cardiac syncope considered the most dangerous type of fainting?

options.A: It is almost impossible to diagnose with standard hospital equipment.
options.B: It causes permanent brain damage within just a few seconds.
options.C: It is frequently linked to serious heart rhythm problems or structural disease.
options.D: It only happens when the patient is actively exercising or working.

explanation: Cardiac syncope stems from heart issues that carry a high risk of sudden cardiac arrest if left untreated. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h2)

question: In Nigeria, where is much of community health nursing practice anchored at the grassroots level?

options.A: Private specialized surgical institutes abroad
options.B: Primary Health Care centers and local outreach programs
options.C: Federal tertiary teaching hospitals exclusively
options.D: Corporate pharmaceutical research laboratories

explanation: Correct! Primary Health Care (PHC) centers are the very heartbeat of community-based healthcare delivery across our local government areas in Nigeria.

question: Why do patients taking lithium need careful guidance about their salt and water intake?

options.A: Salt completely destroys the chemical structure of the lithium pill
options.B: Lithium alters fluid balance and can easily reach toxic levels if hydration shifts
options.C: Water causes lithium to instantly evaporate inside the human stomach
options.D: Patients on lithium lose all sense of taste for salty foods

explanation: Spot on! Lithium handles similarly to sodium in the kidneys, so dehydration or sudden salt changes can dangerously spike drug levels.

question: How do buildings and public places that aren't wheelchair-friendly affect a person with a physical disability?

options.A: It forces them to rely exclusively on online financial investments
options.B: It encourages them to migrate to rural agricultural communities
options.C: It automatically improves their physical strength through daily climbing
options.D: It prevents them from accessing employment, education, and community events

explanation: Exactly. Physical barriers literally lock people out of schools, jobs, and social life, keeping them from living life to the fullest.

question: Why do deep, open wounds heal through 'secondary intention' instead of closing right away?

options.A: Surgical stitches dissolve too quickly in infected tissue environments
options.B: Primary intention only applies to burns and skin rashes
options.C: Secondary intention prevents any risk of bacterial contamination
options.D: There is too much tissue loss to pull the wound edges together directly

explanation: When there's a big gap with missing tissue, you can't just stitch it shut. The body has to patiently build new granulation tissue from the bottom up!

question: What do we mean by 'happy hypoxemia' in COVID-19 care?

options.A: Feeling overly energetic despite severe viral fatigue and muscle aches
options.B: Experiencing extreme chest pain while maintaining normal oxygen levels
options.C: Showing high fever and cough while blood pressure remains stable
options.D: Having dangerously low blood oxygen without feeling short of breath

explanation: You got it! Some patients have shockingly low oxygen levels yet feel completely fine, which is why checking vital signs with a pulse oximeter is so important.

question: Which two drugs are most commonly used together for a medical abortion?

options.A: Oxytocin and ergometrine
options.B: Ampicillin and metronidazole
options.C: Paracetamol and ibuprofen
options.D: Mifepristone and misoprostol

explanation: Great job! Mifepristone pauses the pregnancy, and misoprostol helps the uterus contract and empty safely.

question: What is a major health limitation shared by all traditional and natural family planning methods?

options.A: They do not protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They require daily surgical wound dressing changes
options.C: They cause permanent blockage of the fallopian tubes
options.D: They increase blood pressure above normal levels

explanation: Because traditional methods don't use physical barriers like condoms or chemical germ-killers, they leave users fully exposed to STIs.

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for Meniere's disease?

options.A: Sudden complete ear pain
options.B: Bleeding from the ear canal
options.C: Purulent ear discharge
options.D: Episodic vertigo

explanation: Spot on! Meniere's disease causes sudden, severe spells of spinning dizziness (vertigo), along with ringing in the ears and hearing changes.

question: A community health nurse wants to protect HIV-negative teens who are at high risk of exposure. Which preventive medication should the nurse discuss?

options.A: Emergency therapeutic surgical procedures
options.B: Intravenous antibiotic loading doses
options.C: Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP)
options.D: Immediate lifelong antiretroviral treatment

explanation: Spot on! PrEP involves taking daily anti-HIV medications to significantly lower the chances of catching the virus.

question: Which of these is a true feature of a polysynaptic reflex arc?

options.A: Total absence of a sensory neuron component
options.B: Presence of one or more interneurons
options.C: Involvement of only a single chemical synapse
options.D: Speed that is always faster than monosynaptic reflexes

explanation: Poly means many! These reflexes use one or more interneurons to handle slightly more detailed tasks, creating a few more connections along the path.

question: What is the main reason a fecal impaction forms in the rectum?

options.A: Too much nerve stimulation in the lower spinal cord
options.B: Waste sitting in the bowel too long, losing all its water
options.C: Eating way too many high-fiber foods every day
options.D: Mass movements happening way too fast

explanation: If stool hangs out in the rectum for too long, the body keeps sucking water out of it until it turns into a hard, stubborn rock-like mass.

question: What vital detail must you always include in your nursing notes when a patient passes away?

options.A: The total financial cost of hospital treatment
options.B: The exact time signs of death were observed
options.C: The personal religious beliefs of the nurse
options.D: The name of the nurse who takes over tomorrow

explanation: You got it! Recording the exact time is a legal must-do that shows when care transitioned and starts the paperwork.

question: What is the main reason a midwife uses a partograph while a woman is in labor?

options.A: To monitor the progress of labor and detect early signs of complications
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay
options.C: To measure the mother's daily nutritional calorie intake
options.D: To schedule the exact date for the child's immunization

explanation: Think of the partograph as your trusty labor map! It helps you spot if labor is dragging or if the baby is stressed, long before it becomes an emergency.

question: What is the main underlying problem in cardiogenic shock?

options.A: A massive infection spreading through the body
options.B: The heart pump fails to circulate enough blood
options.C: A severe allergic reaction to dust
options.D: Sudden blood loss from an open wound

explanation: Cardiogenic shock means the heart itself is simply too weak to pump blood forward. It's a pump failure, unlike shock from bleeding where you've lost fluid volume.

question: Why is a patient told to take a deep breath and hold it while a chest or surgical drain is being removed?

options.A: It increases pressure and prevents air from entering the body cavity
options.B: It completely stops the patient from feeling any discomfort at all
options.C: It relaxes the abdominal muscles so the stitches fall apart
options.D: It forces the remaining fluid to rush out before the hole seals

explanation: Holding the breath creates a little bit of internal pressure, stopping air from being sucked into the empty tract as the tube comes out.

question: What makes an 'android' pelvis shape stand out?

options.A: It is heart-shaped with prominent ischial spines
options.B: It is narrow and oval with a very long front-to-back measurement
options.C: It is flat and wide with a short front-to-back diameter
options.D: It is a classic round shape found in most females

explanation: An android pelvis is more like a male pelvis, featuring a heart-shaped opening that can sometimes make labor a bit tricky.

question: Why should a nurse ask non-judgmental questions when assessing a patient's medication habits?

options.A: To trick the patient into admitting they forgot their appointments
options.B: To avoid having to check the pharmacy refill records
options.C: To ensure the doctor prescribes stronger antibiotics next time
options.D: To encourage the patient to speak honestly without fear of scolding

explanation: Patients often lie about missing doses out of fear of being reprimanded by healthcare workers. A warm, non-judgmental approach builds trust and uncovers the truth. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which symptom pattern is most typical for someone with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)?

options.A: Severe sudden constipation that leads straight to a bowel blockage
options.B: Painless bleeding from the rectum every time they pass stool
options.C: Constant bloody stools accompanied by high fevers and weight loss
options.D: Recurrent abdominal pain tied to changes in stool frequency and form

explanation: Well done! IBS is diagnosed when belly pain keeps coming back and is linked with changes in how often and how hard or loose their stools are.

question: Why is promoting homestead gardening a useful nursing strategy against distribution failures?

options.A: It guarantees that families will never need to buy water or soil
options.B: It completely replaces the need for community health clinics
options.C: It reduces a household's total reliance on fragile transport supply chains
options.D: It stops commercial farmers from growing cash crops for export

explanation: Growing food locally around the home provides an independent, reliable source of nutrition when transport systems break down. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h8)

question: Why is government funding for assistive devices like wheelchairs so important?

options.A: It makes devices like wheelchairs and hearing aids affordable for low-income citizens
options.B: It ensures that doctors receive higher salaries than other public workers
options.C: It prevents private hospitals from offering any medical services
options.D: It eliminates the need for physical therapy exercises at home

explanation: Good assistive tools can be very expensive. Government support helps bridge the financial gap so vulnerable patients aren't left behind.

question: Why is an oscillating cast saw safe against human skin during cast removal?

options.A: The saw is powered by low-voltage batteries that stop when touching skin
options.B: The metal blade is coated with a special chemical that repels human tissue
options.C: The blade vibrates back and forth instead of spinning in a continuous circle
options.D: The vibration creates a cooling effect that hardens the skin temporarily

explanation: The oscillating (back-and-forth) motion cuts right through hard plaster, but just bounces safely off soft, stretchy skin.

question: Which two main blood vessel systems supply oxygenated blood to the brain?

options.A: Brachiocephalic and thoracic trunks
options.B: Coronary and pulmonary arteries
options.C: Internal carotid and vertebral arteries
options.D: Subclavian and jugular vessels

explanation: Great job! The internal carotid arteries supply the front of the brain, while the vertebral arteries supply the back. Together, they keep the brain well-nourished with oxygen.

question: Which hormone does the opposite of PTH by helping to lower blood calcium?

options.A: Calcitonin
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Thyroxine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Meet calcitonin, the relaxing counterpart to PTH! Released by the thyroid when blood calcium gets too high, it tells your bones to hold onto their calcium.

question: If a patient scrapes the surface of their skin without a deep cut, which layer took the hit?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat layer
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Hypodermis
options.D: Stratum corneum

explanation: Correct! The stratum corneum is the very top layer of the epidermis, meaning it handles all the daily friction and minor scrapes. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why are non-human reservoirs so important in the spread of diseases?

options.A: They purify local water sources so that waterborne parasites cannot infect people
options.B: They manufacture natural antibodies that help human populations fight off severe infections
options.C: They serve as temporary quarantine stations for individuals exposed to outbreaks
options.D: They provide a safe place for the infectious agent to survive and multiply over time

explanation: Spot on! Reservoirs act like safe breeding grounds for germs, making sure the disease cycle keeps going if we don't intervene.

question: What is a major perk of delaying cord clamping for a healthy newborn?

options.A: It increases iron stores and placental blood transfer
options.B: It makes cutting the umbilical cord much easier for the nurse
options.C: It prevents the baby from developing neonatal jaundice
options.D: It speeds up the expulsion of the placenta from the uterus

explanation: Waiting just a bit before clamping lets that extra, valuable blood flow right from the placenta into the baby, protecting them against early anemia.

question: Because of where the breathing centers are located in the brain, which vital sign must a nurse monitor most closely in pontine injuries?

options.A: Orthostatic blood pressure changes
options.B: Core body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Peripheral oxygen saturation trends
options.D: Respiratory rate and breathing pattern

explanation: Spot on! Since the pons helps control breathing rhythms, keeping a close eye on your patient's respiratory pattern can save their life.

question: A patient arrives at the ward after a knife wound to the chest, and you notice absent breath sounds on one side. What condition should you expect the doctor to treat with a chest tube?

options.A: Pulmonary edema
options.B: Pneumothorax
options.C: Bronchial asthma
options.D: Myocardial infarction

explanation: Chest trauma often lets air leak into the pleural space, causing a pneumothorax that needs a chest tube to let the lung expand again.

question: Why might a surgeon choose external fixation over a standard internal plate for a severe open fracture?

options.A: It allows the patient to remove the metal pins at home every evening
options.B: It avoids placing metal hardware directly into a contaminated wound area
options.C: It completely eliminates any need for follow-up X-ray imaging
options.D: It guarantees that the bone will heal twice as fast as internal surgery

explanation: External frames hold bones securely from the outside, minimizing the risk of trapping bacteria and deep infection inside a dirty open wound. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h5)

question: When would you choose a face mask instead of a nasal cannula for oxygen delivery?

options.A: When the patient only requires a very low flow rate of oxygen
options.B: When the patient refuses to have anything touching their face
options.C: When the patient is completely free of any respiratory distress
options.D: When the patient needs higher and more precise oxygen concentrations

explanation: Face masks cover both the nose and mouth, making them the go-to choice when a patient in distress needs a stronger, concentrated flow of oxygen.

question: Which blood vessels act as control valves to regulate blood flow into local tissues?

options.A: Lymphatic ducts
options.B: Arterioles
options.C: Large arteries
options.D: Vena cavae

explanation: Arterioles have muscular walls that contract or relax to control the volume of blood entering capillary beds. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h3)

question: As women grow older, which health screenings become most important?

options.A: Ovulation tracking and fertility windows
options.B: Congenital anomaly prevention counseling
options.C: Cervical and breast cancer screenings
options.D: Testicular self-examination techniques

explanation: Spot on! Regular checks for cervical changes and breast health are vital preventative steps as women age.

question: How can you deliver holistic care even when working in a busy, understaffed ward?

options.A: By refusing to admit any new patients until the workload lightens
options.B: By delegating all patient contact completely to hospital security guards
options.C: By ignoring all physical medication duties to focus entirely on meditation
options.D: By weaving compassionate communication and a reassuring touch into routine tasks

explanation: Brilliant! Holism doesn't always require extra time. You can easily integrate it into regular nursing duties like bathing a patient or administering medications.

question: Which of these is a major risk factor for getting perineal tears when having your first baby?

options.A: Advanced maternal age
options.B: Short maternal stature
options.C: Nulliparity
options.D: Multiparity

explanation: First-time mothers (in medical terms, nullipara) have firmer tissues that haven't stretched before, making them a bit more prone to tears during delivery.

question: Why is the retina at the back of the eye so important?

options.A: It produces the lubricating fluid inside the eyeball
options.B: It changes color to match the surrounding environment
options.C: It contains cells that turn light into nerve signals
options.D: It acts as a hard shield against physical injury

explanation: The retina holds special cells that catch light and change it into electrical signals for your brain to understand. Great job reviewing this!

question: Why is teaching the family so important before sending a neuro client home?

options.A: Clients with brain injuries never regain their memory or thinking skills
options.B: Family members are legally required to pass a written nursing exam
options.C: Caregivers need to recognize warning signs of complications and manage daily care
options.D: Home health nurses are not allowed to visit clients after discharge

explanation: Since family members will be doing the heavy lifting at home, they need to know what red flags mean it's time to rush back to the hospital.

question: Why is having a skilled birth attendant present during delivery so important?

options.A: They make antenatal visits unnecessary
options.B: They can quickly spot and manage emergencies like heavy bleeding
options.C: They guarantee the baby won't cry at birth
options.D: They prevent the mother from feeling any contractions

explanation: Exactly! Skilled attendants have the training to handle sudden delivery complications and save lives before things get out of hand.

question: What kind of trouble does a nurse face for leaving their duty post without official permission?

options.A: An automatic promotion to a higher administrative grade level
options.B: A commendation letter from the hospital management board
options.C: Immediate conversion of the absence into paid study leave
options.D: Severe administrative penalties for gross misconduct

explanation: Absconding or leaving work without approval is treated as truancy and attracts serious disciplinary action. Always secure your leave first!

question: You need to move a heavy patient from a stretcher to a bed. What is the safest move?

options.A: Ask the patient to jump across while you hold their hands
options.B: Use a mechanical lift and ask another colleague to help
options.C: Pull the patient quickly using your arm muscles alone
options.D: Bend your back completely straight to gain extra lifting power

explanation: Teamwork and mechanical aids save your back! Never try to lift a heavy patient all by yourself.

question: What is a key requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method to remain effective as contraception?

options.A: Taking daily iron supplements along with herbal teas
options.B: Switching to infant formula feeds after the first month
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding without supplementary feeds and no return of menses
options.D: Using male condoms during every third act of sexual intercourse

explanation: LAM relies on frequent suckling hormones to suppress ovulation, but it only works if breastfeeding is exclusive and menstruation has not resumed. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: Which part of the brain releases Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) to kick off the hormone feedback loop?

options.A: Ovary
options.B: Adrenal cortex
options.C: Anterior pituitary
options.D: Hypothalamus

explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the master control center in the brain. It sends out the very first chemical signal (GnRH) to start the whole reproductive hormone cascade.

question: What is the main purpose of wearing a personal dosimeter badge in a radiology department?

options.A: To prove to patients that the diagnostic equipment is clean
options.B: To block radioactive waves from entering the nurse's chest
options.C: To grant the nurse emergency access to locked X-ray rooms
options.D: To measure the accumulated amount of radiation exposure over time

explanation: Dosimeter badges record occupational radiation doses, alerting staff if their exposure levels begin to approach unsafe limits. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why is it strongly preferred to give vasopressors through a central line rather than a peripheral vein?

options.A: Leaking into surrounding tissues can cause severe tissue damage and necrosis
options.B: Central lines deliver medication directly to the kidneys faster
options.C: Vasopressors dissolve peripheral plastic catheters very quickly
options.D: Peripheral veins are completely unable to absorb liquid medications

explanation: Vasopressors cause such intense blood vessel constriction that any leakage outside a peripheral vein cuts off local blood supply and destroys tissue. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is a common sign you might spot in a patient who hasn't been sleeping well over a few days?

options.A: Increased physical strength
options.B: Irritability and confusion
options.C: Hyperactivity and rapid talking
options.D: Heightened alertness to sounds

explanation: When we lack sleep, our brains get sluggish and moody. Patients can easily become easily annoyed, forgetful, or mildly confused.

question: Which type of sleep is mostly connected to dreaming and sorting out memories?

options.A: Rapid eye movement sleep
options.B: Stage one non-rapid eye movement sleep
options.C: Deep metabolic resting phase
options.D: Conscious alpha wave waking state

explanation: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep is that active brain phase where vivid dreams happen and your mind processes everything you learned during the day.

question: What is the job of the sticky adhesive pads that come with an AED?

options.A: Secure the patient firmly to the flat floor surface
options.B: Deliver a continuous supply of medical oxygen to the lungs
options.C: Transmit electrical current from the machine to the patient's heart
options.D: Measure the exact body temperature of the victim

explanation: The pads act as the bridge. They stick to the skin to read the heart rhythm and deliver the life-saving shock safely.
